title: Cody Ponce carted off field after running off mound in Blue Jays debut vs. Rockies
content:
TORONTO — Cody Ponce, in his first MLB start since 2021, was carted off the field during Monday’s series opener against the Colorado Rockies. The Blue Jays’ offseason addition was later diagnosed with right knee discomfort, the club announced. Should Ponce miss time, it could potentially eat into the club’s rotation depth even further.

Ponce ran off the mound in the third inning, grabbing at his right leg as he bobbled a bouncing groundball. The right-hander collapsed beyond first base, grimacing. Ponce was able to get up with help but was ultimately carted away.

Toronto’s rotation, which appeared exceptionally deep ahead of the regular season, has already lost Trey Yesavage (shoulder impingement), José Berríos (elbow stress fracture) and Shane Bieber (forearm fatigue entering spring).

While Yesavage and Berríos are both throwing at the club’s complex in Florida, they aren’t immediately ready to join the rotation. Bieber will throw off a mound for the first time this spring on Saturday and is still weeks away from rejoining Toronto. Berríos will throw a bullpen on Tuesday, and Yesavage is expected to get up to 45 pitches in a simulated game on Friday.

If the Jays need starting help before Berríos or Yesavage are ready to return, they will likely dip into their upper-minors prospect depth. Grant Rogers, Lazaro Estrada, CJ Van Eyk and Chad Dallas are candidates for a promotion, though only Estrada has appeared in the big leagues.

Alongside a partially deferred $210 million deal for Dylan Cease, the Jays signed Ponce to a three-year, $30 million pact this winter to bolster the starting staff. Last year, he was the best pitcher in the Korean Baseball Organization, posting a 1.89 ERA in 180 2/3 innings while striking out 252 batters. Ponce wasn’t expected to bring that level of dominance back to MLB, though the Jays expected him to be a big part of the club’s rotation.

In 2 1/3 innings before his exit, Ponce struck out three batters and allowed one run on one hit. Before he left the game, Ponce fell on the mound when his cleat caught dirt while attempting to pitch. He got up and continued, but collapsed while trying to field a grounder just four pitches later. As Ponce left the field, the 31-year-old buried his head in his arm and screamed.
